chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said:

I wrote to Abi Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom, should I pray behind the one who believes in 'a corporeal body' and the one who follows the position of Yunus, that is, the son of Abd al-Rahman? He (peace be upon him) wrote: Do not pray behind them, nor give them anything of the Zakat, and disassociate from them - Allah has disassociated from them.

key_terms.الْجَسَمِ: Corporeality / Physical body (referring to the belief that God has a physical form)
key_terms.يُونُسَ: Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, a prominent figure in early Shia theological debates

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying behind those who believe in divine corporeality according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Saduq's *Al-Majalis* highlights the theological controversy surrounding Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, a prominent early Shia figure whose views on divine embodiment (al-Jasamiyyah) were deemed deviant by the Imams. The Imam’s directive to withhold Zakat and practice *al-bara'* (disassociation) underscores the practical implications of doctrinal purity in communal worship and financial obligations within the early Shia community.

en.ammaar-muslim: 9. [290/9] Amali of al-Saduq: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. al-Walid from Muhammad b. al-Hassan al-Saffar from al-Abbas b. Ma’ruf from Ali b. Mahziyar who said:

I wrote to Abi Ja’far the Second عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom - should I pray behind the one who believes in ‘a corporeal body (for God)’ and the one who follows the position of Yunus, that is the son of Abd al-Rahman? He عليه السلام wrote: Do not pray behind them nor give them anything of the Zakat. Disassociate from them - Allah has disassociated from them.
